articles.title: South Korea upgrades growth forecast, raises benchmark rates to highest in two years
articles.summary: South Korea's central bank on Thursday hiked benchmark lending rates to their highest in two years, as inflation continues to run above target while a booming economy allows it room to tighten policy. Inflation is expected to remain above its 2% target level for a considerable time, the BOK added in its statement, saying this was due to the pass-through of elevated cost pressures and as demand-side pressures also gradually strengthen, driven by stronger economic growth.

articles.title: K-beauty stocks rally as Korean brands top Amazon bestseller lists globally ahead of Black Friday
articles.summary: South Korean beauty stocks jumped Thursday as the country's skincare brands dominated Amazon's bestseller rankings ahead of Black Friday. Shares of K-beauty giant APR climbed 3.77%, while cosmetic contracts manufacturers Kolmar Korea and Cosmax gained 5.46% and 2.91%, respectively. APR shares, in particular, have rallied sharply this week, up 28%, defying a broader market sell-off in Seoul markets, with the benchmark Kospi index down 2.65% during the same period.

articles.title: Where the market may be mispricing risk most: AI boom, volatility, high-yield bonds
articles.summary: The artificial intelligence boom could lead to a recession, whether through a collapse in AI investment or widespread job losses as the technology advances, a hedge fund manager said. "I do worry that if we don't have an AI-led recession in a few years, we're going to have an unemployment-led recession," Sheru Chowdhry, founder and chief investment officer at DSC Meridian Capital, said during a panel discussion moderated by CNBC's Joanna Ossinger at the iConnections Global Alts Asia conference...

articles.title: Hedge funds are no longer just for the rich. They’re coming for everyday investors
articles.summary: "Heightened geopolitical uncertainty, greater market volatility, inflation concerns, and the higher correlation between equities and bonds have raised questions about the effectiveness of conventional portfolio diversification," said Ricky Siao, a hedge fund specialist at Swiss private bank UBP. The investment environment has become more challenging for investors who have historically relied on traditional allocations to equities and fixed income, he added.

articles.title: Inside India newsletter: Roaring economy, foreign investors’ return and now record auto sales
articles.summary: Despite 2026 being a challenging year with high global energy prices and supply chain disruptions, the Indian economy has fared surprisingly well. India's economy expanded at 7.8% in the June quarter, beating expectations, even as growth in several major economies cooled. The auto industry contributes 7.1% to the country's gross domestic product, 49% to manufacturing GDP, 15% to goods and services tax collection, and supports 30 million jobs, as per government data.

articles.title: Liesman: Why Greenspan could bet on productivity — and Warsh needs to hike
articles.summary: Greenspan famously leaned against inflation hawks on his committee in 1995 and 1996, holding the line on interest rates amid strong growth, because he believed in the productivity promise of the internet revolution. Unfortunately, a quick look at the numbers shows just how different the situation is for Warsh when it comes to inflation, the magnitude of the capital-investment boom and the monetary and fiscal stimulus boosting the economy.

articles.title: SpaceX wins FCC approval to deploy 1 million orbital data center satellites
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission has authorized Elon Musk's SpaceX to put 1 million artificial intelligence computing satellites in orbit, Chairman Brendan Carr announced on Wednesday. Carr said in a post on X, the social network owned by SpaceX, that the company's Starmind constellation, and "competitor constellations will use solar power to extend America's lead" in AI.

articles.title: Nvidia leads tech sell-off as Huang comeback rally fizzles and AI concerns return
articles.summary: Technology stocks fell on Wednesday as excitement over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return faded and failed to calm concerns over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence trade. articles.summary: Meanwhile, some investors say unease surrounding the artificial intelligence trade is partly an emotional or sentiment-driven reaction. Doug Clinton, founder and CEO of Intelligent Alpha, told CNBC's "Closing Bell: Overtime" the AI sell-off is psychological. "I actually think it is difficult to point to some fundamental data point from here that all of a sudden would make investors okay," Clinton said.

articles.title: Nvidia sellers seek new buyers as U.S. curbs China AI chip access, sources tell CNBC
articles.summary: Nvidia chip sellers are seeking new buyers for the semiconductor giant's hardware, three people told CNBC, after the Trump administration tightened rules to curb Chinese companies' remote access to the most advanced artificial-intelligence systems. Jack Duhamel, president of AI infrastructure marketplace GPU Mart, and two people familiar with the matter told CNBC the surge in GPUs for sale was directly attributable to the new rule.

articles.title: Prediction markets push OpenAI IPO expectations later into 2027
articles.summary: Even by October 2027, odds are still only 50-50 that the private company — most recently conducting a funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation — will make its move to the public markets. OpenAI confidentially filed for an IPO in June, but then in an interview with Fortune published in September CEO Sam Altman ruled out a 2026 public markets debut as questions over artificial intelligence safety grew.

articles.title: Anthropic's stock has been a clunker post-IPO. Why that matters for the AI trade
articles.summary: Anthropic shares didn't even rally on Monday, when most stocks in the AI trade ripped higher on news of Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia as CEO. That's the main cloud over the AI trade stemming from Anthropic's stock price struggles. Nevertheless, investors are understandably trying to draw conclusions about the implications because a financially strong Anthropic is not enough on its own to keep the AI trade afloat.

articles.title: Investors led by U.S. billionaire Todd Boehly to buy Lukoil's oil and gas assets outside Russia, sources say
articles.summary: billionaire Todd Boehly's asset management company Eldridge have struck a deal to buy Lukoil's assets outside of Russia, sources confirmed to CNBC. International Development Finance Corporation and Catena Investments, based in the United Arab Emirates, are also parties to the deal, the sources said. The deal transfers Lukoil's international refineries and other production assets in Bulgaria, Romania, Africa and the Middle East to the U.S.-led group, the sources said.
